claims.text: The trip record and the GPS trace describe the same trip: both carry trip_id TRP-02801, and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-13T08:33:21+08:00 matches the trip_record.started_at of 2026-08-13T08:33:21+08:00, so the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is met.

The deviation is established on the trace: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 26.44 km against an optimal_distance_km of 21.0 km, an excess of 5.44 km, which is 25.90% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass — the excess exceeds 20% of optimal and exceeds 0.8 km absolute — so the deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The governing distance figure is the trace, not the rounded trip_record copy: POL-RD-01 provides that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, the trace governs, and the trace records 26.44 km against the trip record's 26.4 km.

The driver's traffic excuse carries no weight: the only traffic_advisory in the bundle is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload, so no advisory names a road the optimal route traverses or carries a validity window overlapping the trip. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the driver's uncited 'traffic was heavy' statement discharges nothing under POL-RD-08.

No rider-requested detour can be run: the chat_log for this trip holds zero messages, so there is no rider instruction timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor and no waypoint_hint to corroborate. POL-RD-04 is unavailable on the record and the excess is not reduced by it.

No relocation clause applies: trip_record.pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be invoked and the booked optimal of 21.0 km stands as the baseline.

The trip is not pooled: trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12 does not apply and the matched-itinerary baseline does not displace the 21.0 km optimal.

The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs the remedy and POL-RD-11 does not: fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so the distance-and-time refund route is open to the rider.

The refund is arithmetic: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 28.4) x 1.2 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 33.8024, against a charged_total of 40.71, giving a refund of 6.9076, rounded up to SGD 6.95. The surge multiplier of 1.2 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, the only artifact that carries it.

The refund is not de minimis and does not reach the full-refund share: 6.9076 exceeds the SGD 0.50 de_minimis floor, and 6.9076 is 16.97% of charged_total, well below the 90% full_refund_share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND rather than NO_ACTION or FULL_REFUND.

No ERP or surcharge correction is due: the fare_breakdown carries zero ERP lines and zero airport surcharge, and the trip neither originates at an airport nor crosses a gantry, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing on top of the POL-RD-02 figure and there is no double-count.

The driver's profile does not establish a repeat-deviation pattern: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 191, so the 3-flag and 5%-ratio tests of POL-RD-06 both fail. The POL-RD-06(b) FULL_REFUND uplift and the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral are therefore not available, and the remedy stays at the POL-RD-02 partial.

The rider's profile does not trigger the extra-corroboration rule: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4, so POL-RD-08's rider-side corroboration requirement is not engaged and the trace alone carries the excess.

The GPS trace is not impaired for policy purposes: it has 100.0% coverage, 208 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, zero gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires and no independent corroboration is required for the deviation finding.

The rider's claim is supported by admissible evidence of full weight: the trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown are all COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0, so the deciding facts are carried at full weight and the POL-GEN-02 confidence cap does not push the case below the 0.70 escalation floor.

claims.text: The trip record and the GPS trace describe the same trip: both carry trip_id TRP-02801, and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-13T08:33:21+08:00 matches the trip_record's started_at exactly, so the artifacts are causally ordered and refer to one journey.

The governing distance is the trace figure, not the rounded trip_record copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 26.44 km against an optimal_distance_km of 21.0 km, an excess of 5.44 km. Under POL-RD-01 the trace figure governs where the two disagree, and the excess is measured from it.

Both establishment tests under POL-RD-01 pass on the trace: the excess of 5.44 km is 25.90% of the 21.0 km optimal, above the 20% threshold, and 5.44 km is above the 0.8 km absolute threshold. The deviation is therefore ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence.

The excess does not reach the materiality gate: 25.90% is below the 50% material threshold and 5.44 km is below the 8.0 km material threshold, so this is an established but non-material deviation and the POL-RD-06 repeat-pattern check is not triggered by materiality.

The driver's explanation in his counterparty statement - 'Traffic was heavy so I took another road' - is an uncited external traffic assertion. No traffic_advisory covers this trip window: the only advisory artifact is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0, so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

The missing advisory is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger here: the driver named no evidence ID for any advisory, and an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one. The absence is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it, so the deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

No rider-requested detour can be run: the chat log for this trip carries zero messages, so there is no rider instruction, no waypoint_hint and no road named. POL-RD-04 is unavailable on the record and no distance is excluded from the excess on that ground.

No pickup or dropoff relocation applies: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be invoked and the booked optimal of 21.0 km remains the baseline.
The fare model is METERED, not upfront: fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-refund route and POL-RD-02 governs the remedy.
The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply and the baseline is the ordinary optimal route of 21.0 km rather than any matched-itinerary figure.

The GPS trace is not impaired for policy purposes: it carries 208 fixes at a 10 second sample interval with 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires and no independent corroboration is required to establish the deviation.

The recomputed fare on the optimal route is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 21.0 + 0.28 x 28.4) x 1.2 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = 33.8024 SGD, using the surge_multiplier of 1.2 read from the fare_breakdown and the optimal duration of 28.4 minutes from the trip_record.

The refund is charged_total of 40.71 less the recomputed fare of 33.8024 = 6.9076 SGD, rounded up to 6.95 SGD payable. That is above the 0.50 SGD de minimis floor and well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 6.95 SGD.

No ERP or toll pass-through correction is due: the fare_breakdown carries zero ERP lines and the optimal route ERP is 0.00, so there is no off-route gantry charge to refund separately under POL-RD-09 and nothing to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

The driver's profile does not support a repeat-deviation finding: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 191 completed_trips_90d, so neither limb of the POL-RD-06 pattern test is met and no conduct referral or FULL_REFUND uplift follows. I note the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure.

The rider's profile does not add a corroboration requirement: deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4, so the POL-RD-08 rider-history condition is not engaged and the claim stands on the trace alone.

The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, the pickup timestamp is consistent, and the excess of 5.44 km meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The driver has pointed to no artifact and no clause that exonerates any part of the excess.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your claim is upheld in part. The GPS trace for TRP-02801 records 26.44 km against the platform's booked optimal route of 21.0 km, an excess of 5.44 km, or 25.9% of optimal. Under POL-RD-01 both establishment gates are passed (more than 20% of optimal AND more than 0.8 km absolute), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED, and the trace figure governs over the rounded 26.4 km on the trip record (POL-RD-01). The excess does not reach the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gate, so this is an established but non-material deviation.

To the driver: your statement that traffic was heavy and you took another road does not change the outcome. No traffic advisory is on file for this trip — the only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-02801-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 — and you named no evidence ID for any advisory. Under POL-RD-13 the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction, your assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and POL-RD-03 is unavailable on this record; this is not the escalation POL-RD-10(5) describes. No chat message records a rider-requested detour (the chat log holds zero messages), neither pickup nor dropoff was amended, and the vehicle is RYDE_X, not pooled.

The remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 (fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not apply). Charged total: SGD 40.71. Recomputed fare: ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 21.0 km + 0.28 x 28.4 min) x 1.2 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, the only artifact carrying it) + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 33.8024. Refund: 40.71 - 33.8024 = SGD 6.9076, rounded UP to SGD 6.95. That is above the SGD 0.50 de-minimis floor and below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.95.

No separate correction arises under POL-RD-09: the fare breakdown carries zero ERP lines and zero surcharge, so nothing is added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure and there is no double-count. No driver compensation is due: the billed distance (26.4 km) is within 1.0 km of the trace. The driver profile shows 0 deviation flags in the trailing 90 days over 191 completed trips, so neither POL-RD-06 pattern limb is met and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows; the rider's 60-day claim count is 1, below the POL-RD-08 corroboration threshold. The only impaired artifact is the missing advisory, which carries no deciding fact, so every artifact carrying a fact this ruling rests on sits at full weight (1.0) and confidence is not capped below the floor. The monetary effect (SGD 6.95) does not exceed the SGD 8.00 automatic execution threshold, so this provisional ruling executes on issue; either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.
